title: Perseus: Andromeda
subtitle: A princess on a rock, a sea-monster, and a wedding interrupted

learningObjectives.text: Why is Andromeda chained to the rock?

main.author: Pseudo-Apollodorus
main.note: Verbatim passage from the named work/translation; the locator selects this exact local source segment.
main.excerpt: he found the king's daughter Andromeda set out to be the prey of a sea monster

narrativeBlocks.title: A mother's boast, a daughter's price
narrativeBlocks.body: Flying home past the Ethiopian coast, Perseus finds a princess chained to a sea-cliff: Andromeda, offered to a monster because her mother Cassiopeia boasted she was more beautiful than the sea-nymphs. Poseidon sent a flood and a beast; the oracle named Andromeda the price.

narrativeBlocks.title: The bargain at the rock
narrativeBlocks.body: Her parents Cepheus and Cassiopeia can't fight the monster — and can't quite resist the stranger who offers to. Perseus's price is marriage; they accept before he even draws his sword.

narrativeBlocks.title: Monster, meet head
narrativeBlocks.body: When the beast rises from the surf, Perseus fights it — in some tellings with sword and sandals, in others simply by pulling out Medusa's head and letting the Gorgon do the work: the monster turns to a reef of stone.

narrativeBlocks.title: The rival at the wedding
narrativeBlocks.body: The celebration itself is interrupted: Andromeda was already promised to her uncle Phineus, who arrives with armed men to claim her. The reception becomes a battle — ended the same way the monster was ended.

narrativeBlocks.title: The rescue formula
narrativeBlocks.body: Andromeda is the cleanest 'damsel on a rock' story in the cycle — boast, oracle, sacrifice, sea-monster, hero. Every dragon-and-princess tale that follows descends from this shape.

quiz.prompt: Why is Andromeda chained to the rock?

choices.text: Her mother Cassiopeia boasted of surpassing the sea-nymphs — Poseidon's monster must be appeased with the princess
She refused to marry the god Poseidon
Her father lost a war and offered her as tribute

quiz.explanation: The boast against the sea-nymphs is paid by the innocent daughter — a recurring pattern.

quiz.prompt: How does Perseus defeat the monster and the rival suitor?

choices.text: He kills both with his father's thunderbolt
He shows Medusa's head — the sea-monster and Phineus's men alike are turned to stone
He outwrestles the monster then bribes the rival
Athena destroys them in a storm

quiz.explanation: The Gorgon's head does the fighting — the ultimate reuse of a trophy.
